subject: biology
title: Adrenaline, thyroxine and negative feedback
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) Adrenaline prepares the body for fight or flight. Thyroxine stimulates the basal metabolic rate. Thyroxine level is kept steady by negative feedback: a change causes a response that reverses it.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Adrenaline is produced by the adrenal glands in times of fear or stress. It prepares the body for "fight or flight".

items.meaning: The endocrine glands that release adrenaline into the blood.
The body's response to danger, getting ready to fight or run away.

items: Adrenaline travels dissolved in the blood plasma to its target organs.
It increases heart rate and blood pressure, so more blood flows to the muscles.
This boosts the delivery of oxygen and glucose to the brain and muscles.
Adrenaline makes liver cells convert glycogen into glucose, which is released into the blood.
More glucose and oxygen means a faster rate of respiration, releasing more energy for muscle contraction.
It also widens the air passages and increases breathing rate.
It reduces blood flow to the skin (vasoconstriction), so less blood is lost from a cut.
Adrenal glands release adrenaline in fear or stress.
It increases heart rate and the delivery of oxygen and glucose to muscles.
More respiration releases more energy for muscles.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Thyroxine is released by the thyroid gland. It stimulates the basal metabolic rate.

items: The basal metabolic rate is the rate of the chemical reactions in the body at rest.
A higher metabolic rate generates more heat.
Thyroxine plays an important role in growth and development.
Someone with an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) makes less thyroxine and generates less heat, so they tolerate cold less well.

diagram.alt: Sort statements into adrenaline and thyroxine.
diagram.prompt: Which hormone does each statement describe?

items.text: Released in times of fear or stress
Boosts delivery of oxygen and glucose to the muscles

items: Thyroxine comes from the thyroid gland.
It stimulates the basal metabolic rate, which generates heat.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Thyroxine is controlled by negative feedback. A change is detected, and the response reverses it.

items.meaning: A change causes a response that reverses the change and returns the level to normal.

blocks.text: Example: a fall in body temperature

items.text: A decrease in body temperature causes the thyroid gland to release thyroxine.
Thyroxine increases the basal metabolic rate.
Body temperature rises, so less thyroxine is released.

blocks.text: The pituitary link (extra detail: some courses ask for it)

diagram.alt: A loop. Low thyroxine causes the hypothalamus to release TRH. TRH makes the pituitary release TSH. TSH makes the thyroid release thyroxine. Rising thyroxine inhibits TRH and TSH.
steps: Thyroxine rises and inhibits TRH and TSH

items: Negative feedback reverses a change and returns the level to normal.
Falling temperature leads to more thyroxine. Rising temperature leads to less.
Where TSH is taught: TRH, then TSH, then thyroxine. High thyroxine inhibits TRH and TSH.

checks.q: Name the gland that releases adrenaline and give two effects of adrenaline on the body.
checks.a: The adrenal gland. It increases heart rate and increases the delivery of oxygen and glucose to the muscles.

checks.q: Explain how the thyroid gland controls the response to a decrease in body temperature by negative feedback.
checks.a: The thyroid gland releases thyroxine, which increases the basal metabolic rate. Body temperature rises, which decreases the release of thyroxine.

checks.q: Why do people with an underactive thyroid tolerate cold less well?
checks.a: They make less thyroxine, so their metabolic rate is lower and less heat is generated.

worked_example.question: Explain how the thyroid gland controls the response to a decrease in body temperature by negative feedback.
answer_points: The decrease in body temperature causes the thyroid gland to release thyroxine (1).
Thyroxine increases or stimulates the basal metabolic rate (1).
So body temperature increases, which decreases the release of thyroxine (1).
worked_example.tip: Show the whole loop: change, response, then the reversal that switches the response off.

worked_example.question: Explain how negative feedback, involving the thyroid gland, controls metabolic rate.
answer_points: Low levels of thyroxine cause TRH to be produced in the hypothalamus (1).
This causes TSH to be released from the pituitary (1).
TSH causes the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine (1).
As thyroxine levels increase it inhibits the release of TRH or the production of TSH (1).
worked_example.tip: Four of these six points score. Name each hormone and the gland it comes from.

worked_example.question: Hypothyroidism occurs when the body has an underactive thyroid gland. Explain why people with hypothyroidism can have less tolerance to cold conditions.
answer_points: The thyroid releases thyroxine, which regulates the body's metabolic rate (1).
This affects the amount of heat that will be generated or produced (1).
worked_example.tip: Link thyroxine to metabolic rate, and metabolic rate to heat.

worked_example.question:
Adrenaline also affects blood glucose concentration.

Suggest how this is an advantage for the "fight or flight" response.
answer_points: Adrenaline causes glycogen to be broken down into glucose.
This increases the blood glucose concentration.
The glucose is used in respiration, which releases energy.
The energy is used for muscle contraction.
worked_example.tip: Three of these points score. Link glucose to respiration, then to the muscles.

blocks.text: Adrenaline also increases pupil diameter, so the pupils widen.
Heart rate rises during exercise and under the influence of adrenaline.

items: During exercise, muscles respire faster and make more carbon dioxide.
The brain detects the higher carbon dioxide concentration in the blood and sends signals to the heart.
The heart beats faster, so more blood carries oxygen and glucose to the muscles and removes carbon dioxide.
Adrenaline from the adrenal glands also makes the heart beat faster.
Heart rate falls back to normal after exercise.
